description: We are a team of Grade 4 students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. For the “Abandoned, Not Forgotten” challenge, we created a digital storybook using NASA data, images, and resources under the guidance of our mentor Kavya S. It explores spacecraft and rovers, Mars Pathfinder, and Spirit, sharing their missions and discoveries through simple storytelling to preserve their legacy and inspire young learners to explore our Solar System.
summary:
NASA sent many machines and robots into space to explore distant worlds.
Some of these machines were left behind after completing their missions.
They explored the Moon, Mars, and other parts of space.
These machines collected important information and sent it back to Earth.
Even after their missions ended, they remained silent on distant planets.
They became reminders of human curiosity and exploration.
Their discoveries helped us learn more about the mysteries of space.
As part of our NASA Hackathon, we planned to create a storybook about these forgotten machines.
Through this storybook, we aim to bring their untold stories to life and inspire curiosity about space exploration.

Innovation Highlights
Story-based learning: Converts space exploration history into engaging stories.

Forgotten machine discovery: Highlights machines and equipment that remain on the Moon and other celestial bodies.

Educational storytelling: Combines scientific facts with creative narratives.

Visual experience: Uses illustrations and space imagery to make learning interactive.
